description:
MEASURED s473t5e (#1501 round 6 member 2).  The six TIMEOUT files that drive
`t/re/re_tests` --

  t/re/regexp.t  regexp_noamp.t  regexp_notrie.t  regexp_qr.t
  regexp_qr_embed.t  regexp_trielist.t

-- each read 795/110 (905 rows of 2,169) at the 90 s default, 1,264 rows short.
The round's question was whether they merely need a bigger allowance in
`baselines/perl-suite-timeouts.tsv`.  THEY DO NOT.

  re/regexp_qr_embed.t at `--timeout 1200`, `--jobs 1`, quiet box:
      P:2167/2   C: 799/108   TIMEOUT

907 rows instead of 905.  Thirteen times the time bought TWO rows.  So the
allowance is not the issue and no row belongs in the timeout registry: the file
HANGS, at a named place.

THE PLACE: re_tests lines 906-926 are the nested-quantifier
catastrophic-backtracking family, e.g.

    .X(.+)+X    bbbbXXaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa    n
    .X(.+)+XX   bbbbXXXaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa   n
    .XX(.+)+X   bbbbXXXaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa   n

(21 rows, also spelled with `[X]` and `.[X]`).  perl's regex engine has the
super-linear cache; cl-ppcre has neither that nor any backtrack/step limit, so
a NON-MATCHING subject makes it explore 2^n states.

  PROBE (scratch/s473t5e/probe-backtrack.pl), subject `'bbbbXX' . ('a' x n)`,
  pattern `/.X(.+)+X/`, no match:
      n     perl     PCL
      10    0 s      0 s
      14    0 s      0 s
      18    0 s      0 s
      22    0 s      0 s
      26    0 s      4 s
      30    0 s      64 s
      34    0 s      (not reached -- the probe's own 60 s budget)
  16x for four more characters = exactly 2^4.  re_tests' own subject is n=39,
  so ~64 s x 2^9 = about NINE HOURS for one row, and there are 21 such rows.

WHY THE OTHER re_tests DRIVERS GET PAST IT: t/re/regexp_normal.t,
alpha_assertions.t and regex_sets_compat.t each SKIP most rows on their own
preamble (`$::normalize_pat` skips a pattern it did not rewrite;
alpha_assertions skips a pattern without assertions; regex_sets_compat skips
one without brackets), and the backtracking rows are among the skipped -- which
is why those three reach re_tests line 1859/2030 while these six stop at 909.

WHAT IT IS NOT: not a PCL compiler bug (the emission is fine), and not #1036
(no Unicode involved).  It is the ENGINE, i.e. #71's territory -- and it is one
of the few places where the parked PCRE2 spike would change the ANSWER rather
than the speed: PCRE2 has a `match_limit`, so it FAILS FAST with
"regexp match limit exceeded" instead of hanging.  DECIDED Â§s476 keeps
cl-ppcre, so as of today this is a registered non-support, not a fix target.

REGISTRATION: `docs/not-supported.md` "Catastrophic backtracking has no limit"
(added s473t5e), cited from all six files' shortfall rows in
`baselines/row-shortfall.tsv` (1,264 each = 7,584 rows) and from
`re/regexp_qr_embed.t`'s 500 blessed fail rows.

DO NOT: add these files to `--quick`'s skip set.  Each still produces 905 of
its rows inside the 90 s default; skipping them would LOSE that coverage,
which is the #176 failure mode.  And do not register an allowance -- the
measurement above says what it would buy.

IF IT IS EVER PICKED UP: the cheapest PCL-side answer is a STEP LIMIT, not a
faster engine -- a counter in cl-ppcre's closure-based matcher that gives up
and signals, so a pathological pattern costs a bounded amount and reports
itself instead of hanging a whole suite file.  cl/vendor/cl-ppcre is a VENDORED
byte-identical copy of Debian's package (s481a) and must not be patched, so
that would mean a fork or a wrapper -- price it before promising it.
subject: the six t/re/regexp*.t files do not need a bigger timeout -- they HANG: cl-ppcre has no super-linear cache and no backtrack limit, so re_tests' `.X(.+)+X` rows take 2^n (n=30 is 64 s, n=39 is ~9 h) where perl answers in 0 s; 7,584 rows short
